title: What if the asteroid missed?
spoken: What if the asteroid had missed? ... Sixty-six million years ago, a rock the size of a mountain is racing toward Earth. But this time, it passes by. No explosion. No fire. No endless winter. ... The dinosaurs wake up the next morning, and nothing has changed. T-rex stays king for millions of years more. ... And our ancestors? Tiny, furry mammals the size of a mouse. They stay in their burrows, only coming out at night. ... Meanwhile, some dinosaurs keep getting smarter. Troodon already had one of the biggest brains of its time. A scientist once imagined what it could become. Standing upright. Big eyes. Hands that can hold tools. ... Now picture today. Skyscrapers, built by feathered dinosaurs. Rush hour, full of raptors. ... And humans? We never show up. ... One rock. One tiny change in its path. That is the only reason you are here, watching this. ... Follow for more what ifs.

title: What if you fell into the deepest place on Earth?
spoken: What if you fell into the deepest place on Earth? ... You hit the water above the Mariana Trench, and you start to sink. ... Two hundred meters. The sunlight is fading. ... One thousand meters. It's gone. Total darkness. The only light down here is alive. Glowing jellyfish. An anglerfish, with a lantern hanging from its head. ... Three thousand meters. The water is almost freezing, and the pressure is three hundred times stronger than at the surface. ... Keep sinking. ... Eight thousand meters. The deepest fish ever filmed lives at this depth. A small, ghost-white snailfish. Below this point, no fish can survive. ... Nearly eleven thousand meters. The bottom. Down here, the pressure is like eight tons pressing on every square inch of your body. ... And the strangest thing ever found at the bottom of the world? ... A plastic bag. ... Follow for more what ifs.
